Forecast run: Wed, Oct 21, 11:14 PM PDT (the page refreshes this a few times a day).
Each hour: time, direction and speed (knots, g = gust), odds of 12kt or more, regime, waves, tide height in ft with r rising or f falling. OUTFLOW NOT RIDDEN = Squamish outflow, never recommend. OFF DIR = direction does not work at that spot.

Guillermo's own take for Wed, Oct 21 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Quiet Wednesday. The Howe Sound outflow is back and a bit stronger than the page shows: Pam Rocks was NNW 19 gusting 28 at 4am and 17 gusting 24 at 5am. Porteau is the only maybe. If Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north before 9am, go early while the tide is low (6.4ft at 8:15am). The flood after that can flatten the swell.

I’m skipping Squamish. The valley is 7°C colder than Pam Rocks, Pemberton is 4 hPa above Vancouver, and clouds are coming.

Thursday looks like the day: Jericho W 15 to 20 from noon, high tide 14ft at 3:50pm.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 09:30 PM PDT 21 October 2026): Tonight and Thursday. Wind light becoming northerly outflow 15 knots after midnight then diminishing to light Thursday morning. Wind becoming southerly inflow 15 near noon Thursday then diminishing to light early Thursday evening.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 09:30 PM PDT 21 October 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Thursday. Gale warning in effect. Wind light increasing to northwest 5 to 15 knots near midnight and to northwest 15 to 25 Thursday morning. Wind increasing to northwest 25 to 35 early Thursday evening.

Track record, last 30 days: Porteau Cove (scored at Pam Rocks): typical miss 3.21kt, caught 52% of windy hours, 13% false alarms; Steveston - Garry Point Park (scored at Sand Heads): typical miss 2.59kt, caught 80% of windy hours, 23% false alarms; Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal Causeway (scored at Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal): typical miss 2.86kt, caught 61% of windy hours, 34% false alarms; Erwin Park (scored at Point Atkinson): typical miss 2.69kt, caught 42% of windy hours, 17% false alarms. Other spots are not measured yet.
